 This Appeal Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

In this appeal, the petitioners have challenged the judgment and award dated 22.04.2019 passed in M.V.C.No.5611/2016 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore (SCCH-11) ('the Tribunal'
for short).
2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, the husband of petitioner No.1, father of petitioner Nos.2 and 3 and son of petitioner No.4 by name Sanjeev, the deceased, NC: 2023:KHC:41296 on 13.10.2015 while riding t h e m o t o r c y c l e b e a r i n g N o .
K A - 4 0 / L - 5 8 3 a l o n g w i t h o n e D .
K . M a n j u n a t h o n Srinivasapura-Chintamani NH-234 road at about 8.30 p.m., hit by a goods tempo bearing No.KA-01/AE-6567 killing both the rider and the pillion rider at the spot.
The petitioners being the dependants have approached the Tribunal seeking grant of compensation of Rs.25 lakhs.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.
After taking the evidence, the Tribunal awarded Rs.14,14,000/- with interest @ 9% per annum.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement of compensation, the petitioners have filed this appeal on various heads.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri.N.Gopalakrishna, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri.Janardhan Reddy, learned counsel for respondent/Insurance Company.

sentences.text: It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the deceased was aged 28 years NC: 2023:KHC:41296 working as mason earning Rs.15,000/- per month, though the accident took place in the year 2015, the Tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.7,500/- and awarded a lesser compensation.
The compensation under the conventional heads is also on the lower side and sought for enhancement.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the petitioners have not produced any evidence to show that the deceased was doing mason and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
The Tribunal on the basis of the available material on record correctly assessed the income and awarded compensation and he has supported the impugned judgment.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of the parties and perused the records.
8. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident, death of the deceased on account of NC: 2023:KHC:41296 accidental injuries.
The petitioners being the dependents are entitled to claim compensation.

In order to establish that the deceased was doing mason work and earning Rs.15,000/- per month, as rightly contended by the learned counsel for the Insurance Company, the petitioners have not placed any material evidence except the Police records pertaining to the accident.
In the absence of proof of income, the deceased has to be treated as person with no proof of income.
In the year 2015, the notional income of a person with no proof of income will have to be assessed not less than Rs.9,000/-.
The Aadhar card pertains to the deceased points out that the deceased was aged 35 years and these are all the factors which require consideration.

9. In a case of this nature, compensation has to be determined by following the principles settled by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Pranay Sethi and Others1 and Sarla (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC: 2023:KHC:41296 Varma (Smt.) and Others -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation and Another2 so also the principle laid down in Shri Ram General Insurance Co. Ltd.
-Vs- Bhagat Singh Rawat & Ors.3 10.

sentences.text: By applying the said principles, by taking the income at Rs.9,000/- per month with future prospects of 40%, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal expenses and '16' is the multiplier applicable.

Towards conventional heads are concerned, loss of consortium to the wife at Rs.40,000/-, loss of love and affection to the children and father together at Rs.50,000/-; towards funeral expenses and loss of estate at Rs.15,000/- each,
amounting to Rs.1,20,000/-.

Since the claim is of the year 2016, in view of the judgment in Bhagat Singh Rawat's case (supra), 10% has to be added for every three years, since 7 years has (2009) 6 SCC 121 Civil Appeal Nos.2410-2412/2023, decided on 27.03.2023 NC: 2023:KHC:41296 already been lapsed, 20% has to be added to the conventional heads (ie., Rs.1,20,000/- + Rs.24,000/-),
then it comes to Rs.1,44,000/-.
In all, compensation comes to Rs.17,56,800/- as against Rs.14,14,000/- assessed by the Tribunal.
Hence, petitioners are entitled for enhancement of Rs.3,42,800/-, which is the just compensation to which the petitioners are entitled.
Hence, the appeal merits consideration.
